transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We have the cell-phone pilot proposal on the table today. Before we move forward with approving any student-facing procedures, I'd like to hear from each of you on the operational side. Could the teacher, counselor, and technology coordinator each report any operational information or concerns you have regarding the draft proposal — particularly around the open classroom bins for grades 9 and 10 and the September 2, 2026 launch date?

transcript.text: I want to share some operational findings from my own classroom trial. Across all my 9th-grade sections, I recorded 23 phone-related interruptions in just two weeks. I also tested numbered locking pouches, and they noticeably reduced interruptions. Based on that, I recommended in my team notes — which haven't yet been added to the draft proposal — that we run a grade-9-only pilot using one pouch per student rather than open classroom bins for grades 9 and 10.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to raise an operational concern. Two students have active safety plans requiring them to receive time-sensitive messages from their caregivers during the school day. I confirmed the plans with both families this week, but this exception has not yet been entered into the pilot procedure. We need to make sure any phone collection method — whether open bins or pouches — includes a clear protocol for these students before we launch.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical technology dependency. I confirmed with the district systems team this week that the student-information system's phone-registration module will not be ready until September 16, 2026. Our technology change plan requires the pilot to launch with a digital registration record on that date, but the draft proposal still shows September 2, 2026, as the launch date. This means the September 2 date is not operationally feasible from a technology standpoint — we cannot launch without the registration module in place.

commitments.detail: Revise the pilot scope from grades 9 and 10 to grade 9 only, and update the phone storage method from open classroom bins to numbered locking pouches, one per student.
Incorporate a clear protocol for students with active safety plans requiring time-sensitive caregiver messages, ensuring any phone collection method accommodates these exceptions.
Change the tentative launch date from September 2, 2026 to September 16, 2026, to align with the student-information system's phone-registration module availability.
Distribute the revised draft proposal incorporating all three operational updates to the team for final review before student-facing procedures are approved.
